summary: Grist is a modern spreadsheet application designed with a relational database structure, allowing you to link tables and enforce data types. It includes row-level, formula-based access control and uses a portable, self-contained format for your records. It functions primarily as an open-source alternative to proprietary tools like Airtable.
goodFor: Teams and individuals who need the flexibility of a spreadsheet combined with the referential integrity of a relational database, particularly when self-hosting is a strict requirement.
watchOut: It represents a heavy software stack involving both Node.js and Python, which increases the surface area for maintenance compared to flat files or single-binary tools. It also directly competes with established proprietary SaaS platforms, meaning user migration and team adoption may require deliberate effort.
deployNotes: As a containerised application built on Node.js and Python, deployment typically involves running a Docker image behind a reverse proxy to handle TLS termination. You will also need to ensure that persistent volumes are properly configured to retain your spreadsheet data and associated configurations across container restarts.
